text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Sharp drop in Q3 net forces Philips Electronics to restructure. (p1)
- Entertainment company Endemol, to be launched on Nov. 7, seeks Dfl 540 million from market. (p1)
- Pension fund ABP and housing corporations plan large projects. (p1)
- Organisations give up fight against value-dating by banks. (p1)
- Shipbuilder De Schelde wins defence ministry order for two air defence frigates. (p3)
- Ceteco Holding takes over Peruvian chain store Total Artefactors. (p3)
- Royal Dutch Airlines KLM strongly opposes second national airport. (p2)
- Dutch banks rapidly expand analysis departments. (p13)
VOLKSKRANT
- Unions fear Philips will shed 3,000-3,500 jobs after disappointing Q3. (p2)
- Negotiations on Samsung's takeover of aircraft maker Fokker near climax. (p2)
- Food and detergent giant Unilever wins VAT case in European Court of Justice. (p2)
- Music and video chain Free Record Shop buys 80 pct of hotel vouchers organisation Hotelbon. (p15)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Leader of Algerian terrorist organisation G.I.A. arrested in Rotterdam. (p1)
- ABN Amro U.S. subsidiary LaSalle books seven percent higher Q3 net at record $49 million. (p27)
- Government subsidy does not reach long-term unemployed, according to research. (p27)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Economic Affairs minister Hans Wijers sees no need for extra money for nuclear energy research. (p4)
- Fashion chain Peek & Cloppenburg to start experiments to return to profitability. (p13)
TROUW
- Consumer organisation Consumentenbond says bank employees often give wrong information on loans. (p7)
- Labour market recovery continues forcefully, according to Central Bureau of Statistics (CBS). (p7)
